compile.overwrite: An assembly file already exists. All previous code will be overwritten if you re-compile

senderCheck.message: Handler `{handler}` {what} without checking who sent the transaction.
senderCheck.hint: Compare the sender with the owner before changing state: `if (getSender(currentTX.txId) != owner) { continue; }` in the dispatch loop, or `if (currentTX.sender != getCreator()) { return; }` at the top of the handler.

sendWithoutCheck.message: `{call}` is not preceded by a balance or amount check.
sendWithoutCheck.hintAmount: Check the funds first: `if (getCurrentBalance() >= amount) { sendAmount(amount, recipient); }`.

unboundedLoop.message: This loop has no recognisable bound; the condition is not driven by anything the body changes.
unboundedLoop.hint: Count towards a limit the condition tests: `for (i = 0; i < 10; i++) { … }`, or move the work into the `getNextTx` loop so each activation does a bounded amount.

activationBelowGas.message: The worst case costs {cost}, but activationAmount is {activation} SIGNA.
activationBelowGas.messageNoDirective: No activationAmount set; the worst case costs {cost}.
activationBelowGas.hint: Set `#program activationAmount {required}` ({requiredSigna} SIGNA, the worst case rounded up to 0.01 SIGNA).
activationBelowGas.hintLoopCap: Loops were assumed to run {loopCap} times; a loop that runs longer costs more.
activationBelowGas.hintNoSwitch: The contract has no `switch` dispatcher, so the analysis could not follow every path and the real maximum may be higher.

switchNoDefault.message: This `switch` has no `default:`, so unknown methods are accepted silently.
switchNoDefault.hint: Add a `default:` that rejects or refunds, e.g. `default: sendAmount(currentTX.amount, currentTX.sender); break;`.

missing.hint: Pin the compiler: `#pragma version {recommended}` at the top of the file.

differs.message: `#pragma version {found}` differs from the Studio's compiler ({compiler}).
differs.hint: Change it to `#pragma version {recommended}` and re-test, or compile with a matching compiler.

missingOptimization.hint: Set it explicitly, e.g. `#pragma optimizationLevel 2`, so the output does not depend on the compiler default.

noCatch.message: No `catch` handler: after a fatal fault the contract stays dead.
noCatch.messageSends: No `catch` handler: after a fatal fault the contract stays dead, with its balance locked in it.
noCatch.hint: Add a global error handler. Resume: `void catch() { asm { JMP :__fn_main } }` — the faulting transaction was already consumed by `getNextTx`, so the contract carries on with the next one. Wind down: `void catch() { sendBalance(getCreator()); exit; }`.

catchRecurringFault.message: A fault here recurs on every activation and burns gas until the balance is gone.
catchRecurringFault.hintDivision: The `catch` handler resumes at `main`, which runs this division again. Guard it (check the divisor, bound the recursion), move it into a handler, or wind down instead: `void catch() { sendBalance(getCreator()); exit; }`.
catchRecurringFault.hintRecursion: The `catch` handler resumes at `main`, which runs this recursive call again. Guard it (check the divisor, bound the recursion), move it into a handler, or wind down instead: `void catch() { sendBalance(getCreator()); exit; }`.

overwrittenParam.message: `{name}` is a deploy parameter, but this line writes it before `main` runs, so the deployed value is replaced on first activation.
overwrittenParam.hint: Drop the write, or only assign when the slot is still unset (`if (x == 0) { x = … }`) inside `main`.
